title: Boot the DGX Spark without a UKI until Limine is fixed

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: completed: one reproduced defect (stale #13260 stack: hardware test misses deleted hibernation guard without /sys/power/image_size; hibernation call not sudo-refused); three optional notes

leads.summary: A successful limine-mkinitcpio exit does not prove that the new direct-boot kernel or initramfs was built
leads.consequence: If mkinitcpio or installation fails for an individual kernel, the upstream hook prints an error but swallows the per-kernel failure. The migration then installs its machine-wide completion marker and omarchy-migrate marks the per-user migration complete. Later users also skip the rebuild; boot entries may still point to the old or absent kernel/initramfs, so a kernel update can leave a stale or unbootable boot target without a retry. Validate direct-boot entries against installed kernels and retry rather than trusting the wrapper status.
leads.triage: already in Opus (N6); not published; limine-mkinitcpio swallows per-kernel failures; old UKI survives; not a PR defect

leads.summary: Open PR #6840 makes Spark updates fail after this override is installed
leads.consequence: Both PRs are diverged and #6840 currently merges on top of this head without a textual conflict. On the Spark the new configuration selects direct Linux boot, but #6840 checks only the unchanged omarchy-uki.conf (ENABLE_UKI=yes), then searches for UKI references in limine.conf. For a normal direct-boot-only Spark entry it finds none, attempts a rebuild, still finds none and exits 1. Its analyzer calls the verifier before update status/restart, blocking each update. Have #6840's verifier read the effective override and verify direct-boot images instead of treating omarchy-uki.conf as authoritative.
leads.triage: already in Opus (N2); published as optional note

leads.summary: A higher-priority /etc/default/limine setting can silently undo the Spark drop-in
leads.consequence: The package's shell loader and Java loader both read /etc/default/limine AFTER every /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/*.conf. On a machine with an explicit ENABLE_UKI=yes there, the Spark drop-in exists and the migration writes its completion marker, but the hook still builds UKIs and the 20-second delay remains indefinitely. The new test checks only copies of the shipped .d files, not this highest-priority file. Determine the effective value before claiming successful conversion, or explicitly document/support this user override.
leads.triage: already in Opus (N1, reproduced); published as optional note

leads.summary: A preexisting empty or partial boot drop-in is mistaken for a valid override
leads.consequence: If the root-owned file exists but is empty, truncated after an interrupted write, or has an unrelated value, the migration skips its writer, runs the rebuild under the still-enabled shipped UKI setting, and stamps both the machine and user's completion markers. Later migration runs never repair it. Check the effective ENABLE_UKI=no value or repair incomplete generated content. The PR's test exercises only a valid preexisting file.
leads.triage: dropped: source-true but low value; empty Omarchy-generated drop-in has no plausible route

leads.summary: Missing limine-mkinitcpio permanently consumes this user's migration
leads.consequence: On an existing Spark where the optional boot tool is missing at the time of the migration (partial package upgrade, bootloader transition, or later installation), exit 0 makes omarchy-migrate write the user's completion marker while neither the drop-in nor the rebuild occurs. Once the tool is installed, this migration will never run again for that user. A nonzero deferred status, or a later retry path, is needed when the tool is required but absent.
leads.triage: dropped: Omarchy installs always ship limine-mkinitcpio; Opus M3 records the test gap privately

leads.summary: Sleep guard and migration treat an empty or changed file as a successful sleep disable
leads.consequence: A zero-byte generated sleep file or one explicitly changed to AllowSuspend=yes still makes omarchy-sleep-disabled return success; the migration will not repair it and omarchy-migrate records completion. Omarchy hides Suspend/Hibernate and prevents their setup, although systemd did not receive the disabling keys. Inspect the effective setting or at least validate the generated file instead of using mere existence as the capability flag.
leads.triage: dropped: file is Omarchy-managed; existence check matches repo patterns; low

leads.summary: New hardware test can touch real swap and /etc if the guard regresses
leads.consequence: The sudo stub execs its arguments with success. If omarchy-hibernation-setup accidentally loses its sleep-disabled early exit, the test calls the actual production script and can progress through a successful gum stub to real sudo-execed chattr, cp /etc/fstab, tee /etc/fstab, mkdir /etc/limine-entry-tool.d and writes outside scratch. Its later assertion cannot undo those writes. In this head the first check of /sys/power/image_size can also bypass the guarded branch entirely. Refuse all unlisted sudo commands (as the later #13260 commit proposes), redirect paths or assert the guard before reaching side effects, and make the image-size check synthetic.

leads.summary: The boot test implements its own lower-priority config resolver rather than testing the consumer
leads.consequence: The test's bash glob loop does not run limine-mkinitcpio's config loader, nor load the user's /etc/default/limine. A plausible Spark configured with ENABLE_UKI=yes in that file passes the test yet boots a UKI; a regression in upstream config precedence also goes unnoticed. Include a fixture with /etc/default/limine and check the actual loader's effective value.
leads.triage: already in Opus (N1 test limitation); merged into optional note

leads.summary: Open PR #13462's ESP capacity check ignores the direct-boot files this PR starts writing
leads.consequence: The two PR heads diverge and patch-merge without conflict. With this PR's ENABLE_UKI=no, the upstream hook copies vmlinuz and initramfs under /boot/<machine-id>/<kernel-name>/ instead of an .efi UKI. #13462 measures only the largest *.efi to estimate required ESP capacity, even though a Limine EFI bootloader can remain there. The preflight either skips with no .efi or sizes against a bootloader unrelated to the files it must deploy, allowing an update to fill the ESP during a direct-boot rebuild. Add a direct-boot sizing path for the kernel/initramfs the hook actually writes; keep the UKI sizing for other machines.
leads.triage: coordinator verified from #13462 diff (find -name '*.efi', base quattro); Opus also verified (P3); published in optional note

leads.summary: Manual sleep-on instructions omit required privilege and the existing suspend toggle
leads.consequence: The generated file is root-owned from install-time root setup or sudo migration; a regular user cannot simply remove it as the new sentence instructs. Even once removed, Suspend remains hidden if the user's preexisting suspend-off toggle exists, contrary to the unconditional 'returns to the menu' wording. Give sudo rm as #13260's extra commit does and qualify the toggle state.
leads.triage: dropped: sudo wording fixed by fb16cc1e (covered by rebase suggestion); toggle interplay expected

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** This PR carries an older copy of #13260, without its current commit `fb16cc1e`.

### The stacked #13260 commits predate `fb16cc1e`

At this head, `omarchy-hibernation-setup` checks `/sys/power/image_size` before the new sleep guard, and `dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh` asserts the "turned off" message only where that file exists. **Impact:** on machines without it, the test still passes with the guard deleted, and #13260's current test fails against this head's code. The hibernation call in this test also goes through the pass-through `sudo` stub; `fb16cc1e` runs that call with `TEST_SUDO_STATUS=1` so the stub refuses every `sudo`.

**Suggested change:** Rebase onto #13260's current head.

<details><summary>Reproducer</summary>

Run these only where `/sys/power/image_size` is **absent**, for example under `bwrap --tmpfs /sys` (containers usually see the host kernel's `/sys/power`). The script below checks this first. At this head the test's `sudo` stub runs its arguments (`exec "$@"`), and only `gum`, `btrfs`, `swapon` and `limine-mkinitcpio` are stubbed. Without the guard, on a machine that supports hibernation, `omarchy-hibernation-setup` would attempt its real `/etc/fstab`, sleep-hook and mkinitcpio/Limine config writes, limited only by file permissions.

**1. At this head, the test still passes with the guard deleted**

```bash
git fetch origin pull/13426/head pull/13260/head
git checkout --detach e76e954f2ab0c7ba0b04cea0ab14647ac07fd9f4
test ! -e /sys/power/image_size || { echo "run this where /sys/power/image_size is absent"; exit 1; }

python3 - <<'PY'
p = "bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup"
s = open(p).read()
guard = 'if omarchy-sleep-disabled; then\n  echo "Hibernation is turned off on this machine" >&2\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n'
assert s.count(guard) == 1
open(p, "w").write(s.replace(guard, ""))
PY
bash test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
git checkout -- bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup
```

Actual output (sandbox without `/sys/power/image_size`):

```
ok - the DGX Spark sleep setting runs at install and through a migration
ok - the detector matches only the DGX Spark
ok - the DGX Spark setting disallows every sleep operation and leaves other machines alone
ok - omarchy-sleep-disabled follows the sleep setting
ok - the migration applies the setting once, only on a Spark
ok - the suspend toggle and hibernation setup respect the disabled setting
ok - the menu hides Suspend and Hibernate only while sleep is disabled
exit=0
```

**2. #13260's current test fails against this head's unmodified code**

```bash
git show fb16cc1e:test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh >test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh
bash test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
git checkout -- test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh
```

Actual output (same environment):

```
ok - the DGX Spark sleep setting runs at install and through a migration
ok - the detector matches only the DGX Spark
ok - the DGX Spark setting disallows every sleep operation and leaves other machines alone
ok - omarchy-sleep-disabled follows the sleep setting
ok - the migration applies the setting once, only on a Spark
Hibernation is not supported on your system
not ok - hibernation setup says hibernation is turned off
exit=1
```

The same guard deletion made at `fb16cc1e` fails #13260's own test with the same `not ok` line, and unmodified `fb16cc1e` passes all seven assertions.

</details>

<details><summary>Details: merge order</summary>

- `fb16cc1e` and `e76e954f` touch disjoint files, so a tree made of `fb16cc1e` plus this PR's four boot files (what a rebase yields) passes both DGX Spark tests (6/6 and 7/7).
- `fb16cc1e` also adds `|| true` to the hardware test's migration lookup, and a manual note that `omarchy apply hardware` restores the sleep file.
- In a simulation with `git merge-file`, squash-merging either PR makes the other conflict in `manual/36-system-sleep.md` and `dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh`. `omarchy-hibernation-setup` merges without a conflict but ends up with the guard twice. Squash-merging this PR and closing #13260 as included would drop `fb16cc1e`.

</details>

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- With `zz-omarchy-dgx-spark.conf` present, limine-mkinitcpio (limine-entry-tool 1.40.0) reads `ENABLE_UKI=no` last among the drop-ins (sandbox run in C, C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8) and takes its non-UKI path: a `protocol: linux` entry with the same command line, then removal of the old UKI entry and file (source review).
- Fresh ISO installs apply the drop-in through `install/hardware/all.sh`, and migration `1790517230` rebuilds once per machine; a rebuild that exits non-zero writes no marker.
- The detector matches only exact `NVIDIA` / `NVIDIA_DGX_Spark`; near-miss, other-vendor and empty DMI values are rejected.
- Both new tests pass at this head (6/6 and 7/7), and the neighbouring menu, migration, Limine and CLI suites pass at head and base.

</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- **Rebuild-before-marker test:** the boot test's failure case fails the first `sudo` call (the drop-in write), so it still passes 6/6 when the marker is written before `limine-mkinitcpio`. A case where only `limine-mkinitcpio` exits 1 passes at this head and fails on that swapped order.
- **`/etc/default/limine` wins over the drop-in:** limine-entry-tool reads it after `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/`, so an `ENABLE_UKI=yes` there keeps the UKI while the migration still records its rebuild. ISO installs do not set it there; the ordering test covers only the drop-in directory.
- **Other open PRs that assume a UKI:** on an overridden Spark, #6840's boot check would find no UKI for the kernel and exit 1, provided the kernel package ships `pkgbase` (not verified). #13462's ESP preflight sizes only `*.efi` files. Both target `quattro`.

</details>
